races.title: State Senate, District 12
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Nathan Magsig
cands.bio: Member of the Fresno County Board of Supervisors (District 5) since 2017. Former Clovis mayor, on the Clovis City Council since 2001. Previously a youth pastor, California legislative aide, nonprofit affordable-housing executive director and energy director at Fresno EOC. Licensed general contractor. Ran for Congress in 2022.

endorsements.text: Republican Party of California (listed by Ballotpedia for the 2026 race)
California Federation of Labor Unions, AFL-CIO (listed by Ballotpedia for the 2026 race)
International Union of Operating Engineers (IUOE) Local 3 (listed by Ballotpedia for the 2026 race)
Reform California (listed by Ballotpedia for the 2026 race)

cands.gaps: We could not find documented actions by Magsig on data centers, homestead property taxes, foreign or investor ownership of land, growth limits, immigration or H-1B, guns, abortion or school choice. We found no documented statements from him on those topics either. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in any recent cycle. His campaign site lists priorities (oil, agriculture, public safety, wildfire reduction, water supply, local control) but gives no detail on specific policies. Where he was raised is not stated in the sources we had. We found no reporting on controversies or foreign ties.

local.label: Roots 55: His campaign site calls him a Fresno County native and the son of a local pastor, and he has been in elected office in the Clovis/Fresno area since 2001; the pages do not state where he grew up, so the score rests on his adult record there of about 25 years.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Elected to the Clovis City Council in 2001 and later served as Clovis mayor. Elected to the Fresno County Board of Supervisors in 2016 and re-elected in 2020 and 2024. Earlier worked as a legislative aide in the California Legislature, executive director of a nonprofit affordable housing developer, and energy director at Fresno EOC. Holds an MBA and an M.S. in Criminology and is a licensed general contractor.
qual.why: About 25 years of local elected office, including a county board that adopts a budget, plus legislative staff experience and business and construction credentials. He has not served in the state Legislature.
qual.label: About 25 years of local elected office, including a county board that adopts a budget, plus legislative staff experience and business and construction credentials. He has not served in the state Legislature.

back-police-order.evidence: His campaign site says he will fight against anti-law enforcement policies to increase public safety.

cands.name: William Brown Jr.
cands.bio: Libertarian candidate for California State Senate District 12 and a Visalia resident. Marine Corps veteran (2000–2013) who worked as an F/A-18 avionics technician. Contract clinical social worker for the Department of Corrections and Rehabilitation, with a private practice. Ran in the 2025 Assembly District 32 special election. Has held no elected office.

endorsements.text: Listed on the CrowdSourceCarrie Voting Guide (Sway voting group), per Ballotpedia.

cands.gaps: We could not find when William Brown Jr. moved to California, so his ties to the state are not scored. He has held no public office, so there is no record of legislative actions. We found no stated positions or actions from him on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buying, growth and land conservation, H-1B or immigration enforcement, police pay, gun laws, abortion, or school choice and teacher pay. The campaign website's endorsements and interviews sections were empty in the page we read.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.
score.why_money: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: 13 years as a Marine Corps avionics technician with maintenance control and quality assurance roles. Now a contract clinical social worker for the state corrections department and owner of a private practice through his professional corporation. Holds an MSW and an MBA. No legislative or elected experience.
qual.why: He has a business-owner and manager background and a policy-adjacent degree (MBA), but no prior legislative or local elected service, so he lands in the middle range.
